title: Phenotypic analysis of a transgenic Drosophila model of Alzheimer’s amyloid-β toxicity
protocol: Estimate required number of experimental (elav-GAL4/Y; UAS-Aβ42/+) and control (elav-GAL4/Y) flies for the experiments.
Prepare bottles of elavc155-GAL4 flies for collection of virgin females.
Prepare bottles of UAS-Aβ42/CyO or w1118 flies for male collection.
Collect virgin females of elavc155-GAL4 and males of UAS-Aβ42/CyO or w1118 until obtaining sufficient flies for the cross.
Place 15-20 virgin females in plastic vials containing food and maintain them horizontally for 4-5 days to ensure no larvae hatch.
Set up the cross by placing approximately 30 virgin females of elavc155-GAL4 with approximately 15 males of UAS-Aβ42/CyO or w1118 into bottles.
Discard or transfer parental (F0) flies after 4-5 days to increase the number of bottles for culture.
Collect F1 males from the experimental group or control group ten days after setting up the cross.
Anesthetize flies with CO2 gas and carefully sort them against the CyO balancer.
Place 25 male flies in plastic vials containing fly food and maintain the vials horizontally.
Change the vials every 3-4 days to obtain age-matched flies from experimental and control groups for each experiment.
Collect male flies from the experimental group (elavc155-GAL4/Y; UAS-Aβ42/+) or control group (elavc155-GAL4/Y).
Place 25 collected flies into a plastic vial containing fly food.
Maintain vials in a horizontal position and age the flies.
Tap flies onto the bottom of the food vials every 2 or 3 days.
Transfer flies to fresh food vials every 2 or 3 days.
Count the number of dead flies at each interval without anesthetizing them.
Continue scoring ages and numbers of dead flies until the end of the experiment.
Analyze survival using the Kaplan–Meier method.
Collect male flies from the experimental group and age them.
Place 25 flies into a plastic vial containing fly food.
Prepare 5-6 vials for different groups of flies.
Transfer flies to fresh fly food vials every 2 or 3 days.
Tap the flies onto the bottom of the food vials and transfer them to new empty plastic vials marked with genotype and scale representing height from the bottom.
Lay down the plastic vials containing the flies for acclimation for 5 min.
Perform the first trial by tapping the vials against a foam pad or layered Kimtowels.
Stand the vials in front of a white board after tapping to knock the flies to the bottom.
Record the climbing performance of the flies distributed in the vials for 10 seconds.
Gently tap vials containing about 25 flies to knock all flies to the bottom.
Wait for 10 seconds.
Image and count flies in the top, middle, and bottom thirds of the vial.
Place the vials in a horizontal position.
Leave the vials for 3–5 minutes.
Repeat steps 19-a through d for the 2nd through 5th trials.
Transfer the flies back into the original plastic vials containing fly food after the assay.
Maintain the flies by transferring them to new plastic vials with fresh fly food every 2 or 3 days until the next assay.
On day 14, repeat steps 17 through 22 once or twice per week.
Count the flies distributed in the top, middle, and bottom parts of the vials using captured photos.
Calculate the percentages of flies in each part of the vials for five trials per vial.
Calculate the average percentages and standard errors for five or six vials for each genotype or treatment.
Compare the percentages of flies that stayed in the bottom part of the vial among genotypes or treatments.
Perform statistical analyses using Student’s t-test.
Anesthetize the fly using CO2 gas.
Rinse the fly in 100% ethanol to wash out the wax.
Place the fly in an embryo dish filled with PBS.
Remove the proboscis from the fly under the stereomicroscope.
Remove the air sac from the site of the proboscis.
Dissect and remove the head from the abdomen.
Fix fly heads with 400 μl of 4% PFA/PBS in a 1.5 ml microtube at 4°C for 16–20 hours.
Remove fly heads from the 1.5 mL microtube using a disposable dropper.
Place six fly heads into each mesh bag.
Remove fixative from the bags containing fly heads.
Place the bags in tissue processing cassettes.
Set the cassette in the tissue processor and begin processing according to the specified program.
Turn on the cryo-plate to cool the paraffin blocks quickly.
Keep the processing cassettes in a paraffin bath at 60°C.
Place the fly heads and melting paraffin into a stainless base mold on a heat block.
Align the fly heads with the anterior side up.
Transfer the mold containing the fly heads to the cold plate.
Place the tissue cassette on top of the mold filled with paraffin.
Allow the mold on the cooled cryo-plate until the paraffin solidifies (20–30 min).
After cooling, remove paraffin blocks from the mold and keep them at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Turn on the water bath filled with distilled water (38°C–40°C).
Trim the extra paraffin.
Soak the block in distilled water to avoid static electricity during sectioning.
Place the blade (S35, Feather) at an angle of 5°.
Cut sections of fly brain with a thickness of 6 μm serially from the posterior side to the anterior side of the fly head.
Cut the ribbons of sections (10–12 sections).
Float the ribbon of sections on warmed distilled water (38°C–40°C) in the water bath.
Pick up the ribbon of sections using a slide glass.
Stand the slide for more than 12 h at room temperature (20°C–25°C) to dry out the ribbon of sections.
Place the slides in a slide rack.
Soak the slides in reagents for H&E staining as listed in Table 2.
Remove the slide from xylene and place it in mounting media (Multi mount 220).
Cover the fly heads sections with a coverslip.
Observe all slides with serial sections of fly heads under the microscope.
Select the brain section with the most severe vacuolation in the same area of each brain.
Capture an image of the selected brain region using the microscope camera.
Analyze the total cell body area and all vacuole areas in the selected brain region using ImageJ software.
Calculate the percentage of the vacuole area: 100 * (vacuole area / total cell body).
Subject the percentage of the vacuole area in Aβ42 flies and control flies to statistical analyses using Student’s t-test.
Collect male flies from the experimental group or control group and age them.
Anesthetize flies with CO2 gas when they reach the desired age.
Place anesthetized flies in a 1.5 mL tube followed by flash-freezing in liquid nitrogen.
Store flash-frozen flies at -80°C until use.
Extract Aβ42 from fly heads using RIPA/SDS buffer followed by formic acid treatment.
Place the 1.5 mL tubes containing 20–25 frozen flies in a Dewar vessel with liquid nitrogen.
Pick up a tube using forceps and quickly place it into a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Shake the tube to physically divide fly heads from abdomens.
Remove contents of the 1.5 mL tube onto weighing paper on ice.
Collect 20 fly heads in a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add 200 μL RIPA/SDS buffer to the tube and homogenize using a micro-pestle.
Incubate the tube on ice for 1 hour, vortexing every 20 minutes.
Spin the tubes at 16,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant (RIPA/SDS soluble fraction) to a new tube.
Add 400 μL RIPA/SDS buffer to the pellet and vortex.
Spin the tubes at 16,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Add 100 μL of 70% formic acid to the pellet.
Incubate on ice for 1 hour, frequently vortexing.
Spin the tubes at 16,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new tubes.
Evaporate the formic acid using a vacuum centrifuge concentrator.
Resuspend the pellet in 40 μL DMSO (RIPA/SDS insoluble/formic acid-soluble fraction).
Add 10 μL of 2X sample buffer to 10 μL RIPA/SDS soluble fraction per lane.
Add 18 μL of 2X sample buffer to 2 μL RIPA/SDS insoluble fraction per lane.
Heat the samples at 95°C for 2 minutes.
Spin the tubes at 16,000 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Collect the supernatant.
Run SDS-PAGE using Novex Tris-Tricine 10%–20% gradient gel.
Transfer proteins onto nitrocellulose membrane using an XCell II™ Blot Module.
Boil the membrane in PBS for 3 minutes.
Block the membrane with 5% skim milk in TBST for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the membrane with TBST for 5 minutes.
Incubate the membrane with anti-Aβ antibody (6E10, 1:4,000) at 4°C for 16–20 hours.
Wash the membrane with TBST for 3 times, each time for 5 minutes.
Incubate the membrane for 2 hours at room temperature (20°C–25°C) with anti-mouse IgG antibody conjugated to HRP at a dilution of 1:4,000.
Wash the membrane with TBST for 3 times, each time for 5 minutes.
Incubate the membrane with ECL reagent.
Detect Aβ using a chemiluminescence image analyzer.
Boil the nitrocellulose membrane in PBS for 3 minutes to increase the reactivity of Aβ42 to the anti-Aβ antibody (6E10).
Collect male flies from the experimental group and age them until the desired age is reached.
Dissect the brains of flies under a stereomicroscope with light sources after anesthetizing them using CO2 gas.
Rinse the fly in 100% ethanol to wash out the wax, and place it in an embryo dish filled with PBS.
Fix fly brains in 400 μL of 4% PFA/PBS for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Remove fixative from the fixed brain samples.
Rinse the brain samples three times with PBST.
Wash the brain samples with PBST twice, each time for 10 minutes to permeabilize.
Remove PBST.
Add 200 μL of 10% formic acid and incubate with gentle shaking for 1 h at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash with PBST (2 × 10 min).
Remove the PBST and add 100 μL blocking solution (10% NGS/1% Triton X-100/PBS).
Incubate and gently shake for at least 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 0.5 μL anti-Aβ antibody (82E1, 1:200) to the tube containing blocking solution.
Rotate in the dark at 4°C at least 16 h (this step can be 2–3 days).
Remove primary antibody reaction mixture and rinse three times with PBST.
Wash with PBST (3 × 15 min with gentle shaking).
Remove the PBST and add 100 μL blocking solution.
Incubate and gently shake for at least 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 0.2 μL Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG antibody (1:500) to the tube containing blocking solution.
Rotate in the dark at 4°C at least 16 h (this step can be 2–3 days).
Remove secondary antibody reaction mixture and rinse three times with PBST.
Wash with PBST (3 × 15 min with gentle shaking).
Rinse with PBS.
Rinse with 50% glycerol/PBS.
Transfer the fly brains to the center of the reinforcement label on the cover slip and align them, keeping the anterior side up.
Remove excess solution and fill with antifade mounting media (SlowFade Gold).
Cover the brains with a 15 mm diameter round glass cover slip.
Seal the edge of the coverslip with nail polish.
Aspirate away the fixative and wash fly brain samples with 500 μL PBST (2 × 5 min).
Remove the PBST and stain the fly brains with 100–200 μL of 0.002% FSB in 50% ethanol solution for 30 min at room temperature in the dark.
Remove the FSB solution and rinse twice with saturated lithium carbonate solution.
Rinse twice more with 50% ethanol.
Mount fly brain samples for imaging.
Acquire images by confocal microscopy using the filter set for DAPI.
